▲ EL. 6,100 FT The ground under your slab

Three things in this dirt want your driveway gone. We plan for all three.

  1. Reading 01 · Clay

    It swells when wet

    Expansive clay lifts and drops a slab with every wet spring. We dig past it and lay a thicker, compacted base so it has less to push.

  2. Reading 02 · Frost

    It freezes, thaws, refreezes

    Sunny afternoons and frozen nights put the slab through the cycle again and again. Air bubbles in the mix give the ice room to grow.

  3. Reading 03 · Salt

    It rides in on your tires

    Magnesium chloride from the roads drips off every car all winter. A fall seal keeps it out of the surface.

▲ EL. 6,200 FT One January night

Why a driveway here flakes after one winter

Concrete that was fine in a warm state peels here. It happens in four steps, and the fix is built in on pour day.

  1. 01 · Melt

    Deicer melts the ice and pulls salty water into the top quarter inch of the slab.

  2. 02 · Freeze

    The night drops well below freezing. Water in the pores turns to ice and grows about nine percent.

  3. 03 · Scale

    With nowhere to go, the ice pops the top layer off in flakes and the stone shows through.

  4. 04 · Built in

    Air-entrained mix leaves millions of tiny voids for the ice. A fall seal keeps the salt water out.

▲ EL. 6,600 FT Under the slab

What you cannot see does the work

Slab
5 in. for driveways, 4 in. for walks and patios
Base
4–6 in. compacted road base, deeper where the clay tests high
Steel
#4 rebar on chairs at 18 in. on center
Mix
4,000 psi, air-entrained, low slump
Joints
Saw-cut within hours of the pour, 10–12 ft apart, ¼ of the slab deep
Slope
⅛ in. per foot, away from the house

Repair, lift or replace? Two quick reads

Pick what your slab looks like, or tick what is true. You will know what to ask for before we come look.

Which looks most like your slab?

▲ Waiting

Pick the closest match.

Your read shows up here, with what we would do about it.

Seal

Crazing: surface only

Fine hairline cracks from fast drying. Usually cosmetic. Clean and seal it in the fall.

Watch

The joint did its job

A crack inside a cut joint is planned. Fill the joint so water stays out, and keep an eye on it.

Lift

Settled panel: lift it

Soil under it washed out or settled. If the panel is still in one piece, lifting is usually enough.

Repair / replace

Scaling from salt and frost

Light scaling can be resurfaced. Deep scaling over most of the slab means a new pour with air in the mix.

Repair

Popouts: a weak stone froze

A soft stone near the top took on water and burst. Patch the craters and seal the surface.

Replace panel

Heave from roots or clay

Something underneath is pushing up. We replace the panel and check the base before we pour again.
